basis: Vitamin deficiency disorder; affected organs vary across B-vitamin deficiencies, with no additional organ consistently damaged across the umbrella.
MS4A1-associated antibody immunodeficiency; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic airway or lung damage.
Spinal cord lipoma; the usual dysraphic form includes a communicating subcutaneous lipoma, supporting subcutis involvement in most cases.
Upper motor neuron degeneration causes spastic weakness and bulbar dysfunction; these do not establish separate muscle or gastrointestinal disease.
Specific phobia is a psychiatric condition without defining damage to an organ axis.
Iron accumulation disorder; sites vary across subtypes, and deposition alone does not establish organ dysfunction.
Malignant tumor arising in the orbit; myoblastic differentiation does not establish additional skeletal muscle involvement.
Congenital cardiac outflow obstruction. The laryngeal-stenosis annotation conflicts with the defined condition and is not accepted as typical involvement.
Inherited intestinal brush-border enzyme deficiency impairs sucrose digestion and carbohydrate metabolism.
Thelazia nematodes occupy the conjunctival sac and lacrimal system, causing ocular infection.
Premature fusion of one frontosphenoidal skull suture; neurologic or visual damage is not established as common in this nonsyndromic form.
Defining renal, hepatic and pancreatic dysplasia; renal failure and cirrhosis each reported in 2/2 patients; pancreatic fibrosis and cysts affect exocrine tissue.
Obesity with chronic alveolar hypoventilation and respiratory failure; associated sleep apnea and secondary cardiovascular diagnoses are assessed separately.
Defining skin, eye and CNS abnormalities; anemia occurs in 30-79%. Dental/palatal and joint abnormalities also frequent but omitted under the four-axis cap.
Clonal mast-cell marrow neoplasm; persistent skin infiltration in ~70-80%; skeletal remodeling and bone loss in ~30-50%. GI symptoms alone do not prove tissue damage.
Benign mesothelial tumor confined to the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Benign cystic lesion of bone; fractures remain within the skeletal axis, and neurologic abnormalities are very rare.
Destruction of central or peripheral neuronal myelin; immune mechanisms apply to some subtypes rather than the entire umbrella.
Substance-use disorder; no specific organ injury is intrinsic to the supplied concept.
Inherited purine-metabolism enzyme disorder; the supplied syndromic synonym identifies deafness and neurologic ataxia as defining manifestations.
Inflammatory pituitary disorder with macrophage and giant-cell accumulation and fibrosis; supports endocrine and immune-mediated involvement.
HSV-1 infection producing characteristic genital mucocutaneous lesions; neurologic complications are uncommon.
Congenital external auditory canal obstruction with conductive hearing loss and associated middle-ear abnormalities.
CEP135-associated primary microcephaly with severe intellectual disability in 2/2 patients; craniofacial shape does not establish separate skeletal disease.
Hyperplasia of urinary tract urothelium; possible association with later neoplasia does not add another organ axis.
